A galaxy of information inequalities, with applications

Thomas Courtade
Associate Professor, UC Berkeley
Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 4:00 PM • Packard 202

Abstract

This talk will attempt to summarize some recent developments in information inequalities, with an emphasis on unifying perspectives. In particular, I’ll present a general class of information-theoretic inequalities that all follow from a single, unified isoperimetric-type principle. To the extent that time allows, I’ll try to demonstrate a variety of applications to information theory, analysis, statistics (and more?).

Bio

Thomas Courtade is an Associate Professor in EECS at the University of California, Berkeley. His research interests span information theory and its applications. In recent years, he’s focused on exploring problems at the intersection of information theory and mathematics, with a particular emphasis on limit theorems, functional inequalities, and extremal properties.
